questions.question: Can you show who ultimately owns and controls each critical supplier, and when that was last checked?
evidence: A beneficial ownership record for each critical supplier, with its source and date
Sanctions screening results against the UK, EU and US lists
A re-screening schedule, and evidence of its last run
questions.warning: Ownership was captured once at onboarding and never refreshed.
anchored: Home Office guidance on failure to prevent fraud (due diligence)
OFSI and OFAC sanctions guidance

questions.question: Does each supplier contract give you the right to obtain the documents your own regulators may ask for, including the supplier's export filings?
evidence: A contract clause on record access and retention
A test request made to a supplier, and the answer it produced
A list of suppliers whose contracts lack the clause
questions.warning: The right is assumed, and has never been exercised.
anchored: ISO 9001:2015 clause 8.4.3, Information for external providers
CBP advance notice on supply chain visibility, September 2026

questions.question: When a supplier changes factory, sub-supplier or ownership, how do you find out, and how quickly?
evidence: A contractual duty on the supplier to notify changes
A change log comparing the date notified with the date the change took effect
The re-assessments each change triggered
questions.warning: Changes are discovered from shipping documents after the goods have moved.
anchored: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A 5.22, Monitoring, review and change management of supplier services
ISO 9001:2015 clause 8.4

questions.question: Which suppliers are rated high risk, on what criteria, and does the rating change what you check?
evidence: Documented risk criteria and the resulting supplier tiers
Evidence that high-risk suppliers receive extra checks, such as audits or sampling
The date each rating was last reviewed
questions.warning: Every supplier answers the same questionnaire, whatever its risk.
anchored: Home Office guidance on failure to prevent fraud (risk assessment, proportionate procedures)

areas.title: What the goods are, and where they come from

questions.question: For a sample of imports, can you trace the declared country of origin back to evidence from the producer?
evidence: Supplier origin declarations covering the goods and dates
The bill of materials and the processing location for the goods
A record of your own review before the origin was declared
questions.warning: Origin is copied from the commercial invoice.
anchored: 19 CFR Part 134, country of origin marking
UK–EU Trade and Cooperation Agreement, rules of origin chapter

questions.question: If you claim preferential duty under a trade agreement, who holds the evidence behind the claim, and could you produce it within days?
evidence: Supplier declarations with their validity periods
The file supporting any claim made on the importer's knowledge
Verification requests received, and how they were answered
questions.warning: Preference is claimed by the broker by default, and nobody holds the evidence.
anchored: UK–EU Trade and Cooperation Agreement, rules of origin chapter

questions.question: Who signs off the tariff classification of a new product, and is the reasoning written down?
evidence: Classification decisions recorded with their rationale
Advance tariff rulings, where obtained
A trigger to review the classification when the product specification changes
questions.warning: The classification is inherited from the supplier's paperwork.
anchored: HMRC Advance Tariff Rulings
World Customs Organization Harmonized System

questions.question: Can you show that inputs at high risk of forced labour were checked before you bought them?
evidence: Screening of inputs by product and region
Traceability from the finished product back to its raw materials
A product-level evidence file for each high-risk product
questions.warning: There is a policy statement and a supplier code of conduct, and no evidence at product level.
anchored: Modern Slavery Act 2015, section 54
EU Forced Labour Regulation (EU) 2024/3015, applying from 14 December 2027
US Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act

areas.title: Documents that must agree
areas.sub: Reconciling the record with the goods

questions.question: For a sample of shipments, do the purchase order, commercial invoice, packing list, customs entry and goods receipt agree on quantity, value and description?
evidence: Reconciliation workpapers for the sample
A log of the differences found
How, and by whom, each difference was closed
questions.warning: Each document is checked by a different team, and nobody compares them.
anchored: ISO 9001:2015 clause 8.4.2, Type and extent of control

questions.question: When the price paid differs from the value declared, who corrects the customs declaration?
evidence: A procedure for post-entry amendments and disclosures
Examples of corrections made after price adjustments, rebates or assists
A routine report from finance to trade compliance
questions.warning: Price adjustments are settled in finance and never reach customs.
anchored: HMRC Notice 252, valuation of imported goods
19 CFR 162.74, prior disclosure

questions.question: Could you produce the full record for any entry from the last five years, including the documents your broker holds?
evidence: A retention policy by record type
A test retrieval of randomly chosen entries
The broker's retention and hand-back terms
questions.warning: The records sit with the broker, and nobody has ever asked for them.
anchored: 19 CFR Part 163, recordkeeping
HMRC customs record-keeping requirements

questions.question: Are goods received checked against what was declared to customs as well as against the purchase order?
evidence: Goods-in checks against the shipping documents
Discrepancy reports routed to trade compliance
Examples where a short or substituted delivery led to a corrected declaration
questions.warning: Short or substituted goods are resolved with the supplier and never with customs.
anchored: 19 CFR 162.74, prior disclosure
ISO 9001:2015 clause 8.6, Release of products and services

questions.question: When procurement onboards a supplier, what does trade compliance receive, and when?
evidence: The workflow showing the hand-off and its timing
The checklist trade compliance completes
Examples where trade compliance stopped or changed an onboarding
questions.warning: Trade compliance learns about a new supplier from its first shipment.
anchored: UK Corporate Governance Code 2024, Provision 29 (material controls)

questions.question: If receiving, finance and customs each record a different quantity, whose figure prevails, and who records why?
evidence: A defined escalation route for mismatches
Three-way match exceptions and their resolution
A decision log naming who decided
questions.warning: The difference is written off without anyone tracing which record was wrong.
anchored: ISO 9001:2015 clause 10.2, Nonconformity and corrective action

questions.question: Who owns each control that spans two teams, by name, and does each team know it?
evidence: A control register with a named owner for every cross-team control
Owner attestations or sign-offs
Evidence that both teams were told
questions.warning: The register lists a team or a system as the owner.
anchored: UK Corporate Governance Code 2024, Provision 29
ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A 5.2, Information security roles and responsibilities

questions.question: When someone in the chain leaves or changes role, how are their supplier knowledge and open issues handed over?
evidence: Handover records for leavers and movers
Timely removal of system access
Open exceptions reassigned to a named person
questions.warning: Open issues leave with the person.
anchored: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A 5.11, Return of assets, and 6.5, Responsibilities after termination or change of employment

questions.question: What instructions does your customs broker work from, and when did you last review what it declared in your name?
evidence: Written broker instructions covering classification, valuation, origin and preference
A periodic review of a sample of the broker's entries
The findings of that review, and what changed
questions.warning: The broker's entries are trusted because they have never been questioned.
anchored: 19 CFR Part 111, customs brokers
Home Office guidance on failure to prevent fraud (associated persons)

questions.question: Which agents, forwarders and intermediaries act on your behalf, and are they covered by your fraud and bribery procedures?
evidence: A register of associated persons
Contract clauses and due diligence for each
Training or attestations, where proportionate
questions.warning: The register covers suppliers and leaves out the intermediaries.
anchored: Economic Crime and Corporate Transparency Act 2023, section 199
Bribery Act 2010, section 7

questions.question: Can you see the evidence your logistics providers hold about where your goods were, and when?
evidence: Access to tracking and custody data, with its retention period
Exception reports for delays, transfers and seal breaks
Terms for handing the data back when the contract ends
questions.warning: Custody data exists only in the provider's system and disappears with the contract.
anchored: ISO 28000:2022, Security and resilience: security management systems

areas.title: Data and technology
areas.sub: From the triangle: IoT, AI and the record

questions.question: Where sensor or tracking data supports a compliance claim, how do you know the device was working and the data unaltered?
evidence: Device calibration and health records
Integrity controls on the data as it moves
Logs of who accessed or changed it
questions.warning: The data is accepted because it came from a machine.
anchored: ISO/IEC 27400:2022, IoT security and privacy
ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A 8.15, Logging

questions.question: If an AI or automated tool screens suppliers, transactions or documents, who reviews its results, and how are its errors found?
evidence: An inventory of the tools and what each decides
Records of human review
Testing for missed cases and false alarms, and a change log for the rules or models
questions.warning: Nobody can say what the tool has missed.
anchored: EU AI Act, Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, where the use is in scope

questions.question: For records shared on a common platform or ledger, who can write to them, and can a correction be told apart from the original entry?
evidence: Defined write permissions
An audit trail that keeps the original alongside each amendment
Reconciliation of the shared record with the source documents
questions.warning: Corrections overwrite the record and leave no trace.
anchored: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A 5.33, Protection of records, and 8.15, Logging

questions.question: Where personal data is collected along the chain, from drivers, workers or sensors, are its purpose and retention defined?
evidence: Records of processing that cover supply chain data
Privacy notices for the people concerned
A retention schedule, and evidence it is applied
questions.warning: Location and identity data is kept indefinitely because it might be useful.
anchored: UK GDPR, Article 30
ISO/IEC 27701

questions.question: Is there one log of the exceptions found across procurement, receiving, finance and customs, and does anyone review it?
evidence: An exceptions log with owner, root cause and closure date
Minutes of the reviews that considered it
Trends reported to management
questions.warning: Each team keeps its own list, and nobody sees the pattern.
anchored: ISO 9001:2015 clause 9.3, Management review
Home Office guidance on failure to prevent fraud (monitoring and review)

questions.question: When an error is found in past declarations, how is the decision made to correct or disclose it, and how quickly?
evidence: A written correction and disclosure procedure
Records of each decision and who made it
Time taken from discovery to correction
questions.warning: Errors are fixed for future shipments and never corrected for past ones.
anchored: 19 CFR 162.74, prior disclosure
HMRC guidance on correcting errors in import declarations
